Hi Mark / Asha,

Appreciate the detail — that's perfect. I've attached our MAP_token_econ_workbook_v2.xlsx and a short PDF summary. The workbook includes a small traffic simulator so you can toggle average response tokens, cache hit rate, and batching to see tokens/$ impact.

Quick answers up front:
- Knobs: batch size (we recommend 4–8 for low-latency POCs), model quantization (q4 reduces GPU token cost ~35–55% depending on model), and prefix/KV cache (saves when you have repeated/persistent context between sessions).
- Baseline calc we use in the workbook: effective tokens per $ = (1 / per_token_cost). Per_token_cost = GPU_inference_cost_per_hour / (tokens_per_second * seconds_per_hour * utilization). We provide typical ranges in the sheet.

Subject: Re: MAP token economics — draft numbers for MediCura

Stephanie / Neha — drafted a quick set of assumptions and a worked example you can paste into the MAP workbook. Numbers are conservative for Dedicated GPU pricing with a quantized 13B-class model; adjust if they select hosted or a larger model.

Assumptions (POC baseline):
- Model profile: 13B quantized (q4h), serving on A100-class GPU equivalent.
- Avg prompt tokens: 60
- Avg response tokens: 260
- Avg tokens per interaction = 320
- Batch size: 6 (continuous batching with a 20 ms coalesce window)
- KV/prefix cache hit rate: 12% (savings applied only to generation tokens)
- Utilization: 70% steady-state for POC

Raw numbers (worked):
- Measured tokens/sec per GPU (single-stream equivalent, with batching 6): 820 tokens/sec
- Effective tokens/sec at utilization 70% = 574 tokens/sec
- Tokens per hour = 574 * 3600 = 2,066,400 tokens
- If GPU inference cost (ops-only) = $24/hour (example Dedicated run rate in workbook), per_token_cost = 24 / 2,066,400 = $0.00001161/token
- Tokens per $ = 1 / per_token_cost ≈ 86,100 tokens per $
- Apply cache savings (12%): effective tokens/$ ≈ 97,840 tokens per $ (since fewer tokens billed per interaction)
- Per-interaction cost (avg interaction 320 tokens) = 320 * 0.00001161 ≈ $0.0037 per interaction

Notes and sensitivities (for MAP):
- Batching: increasing batch size to 12 raises tokens/sec to ~1200 in our perf tests, lowering per-token cost by ~28% but increases p95 latency by ~70–120 ms depending on request inter-arrival.
- Quantization: moving from fp16 -> q4h reduces per-token GPU time ~40% in our internal kernels; validation in the POC is required to confirm quality parity.
- Cache: prefix caching benefits depend heavily on prompt reuse. If the product uses a lot of short system/context messages repeated across requests, cache hit can be 20–30% and materially reduce cost.

Suggested gating values to include in the MAP (pass/fail):
- Token economics gate: modeled tokens/$ within +/-15% of measured at 48-hour steady-state run (critical).
- Latency gate: p95 generation latency under chosen model <= 700 ms (or define per-route)
- Quality gate: human-eval quality delta <= 3% compared to baseline (we'll supply eval harness)
- Stability gate: error rate < 1% over 24-hour smoke run

I'll paste a compact table you can include in the MAP summary.

-Ben

Hi Mark / Asha —

Attached is the draft MAP with the token economics appendix filled out (MAP_token_econ_workbook_v2.xlsx) plus a two-page summary (redwood_map_summary.pdf). Highlights below for quick review:

Executive summary:
- Expected per-interaction cost (baseline assumptions): $0.0037 (avg 320 tokens) with batching=6, q4 model, 12% cache hit.
- Projected tokens per $ (baseline) ≈ 86k tokens/$; with cache applied ≈ 98k tokens/$.
- Sensitivity: increasing batch to 12 reduces cost ~28% but may increase p95 by 70–120ms.

MAP acceptance gates (what we suggest MediCura sign):
1) Tokens/$ verification: modeled vs measured tokens/$ must be within +/-15% after a 48-hour run using the same traffic profile.
2) Batching validation: confirm p95 latency change < 150 ms for batching levels up to 12 (test window included).
3) Cache validation: confirm prefix/KV cache hit >= 10% for the main demo flows, or document why lower.
4) Quality regression: automatic A/B on a 200-sample eval set; quality delta (clarity/accuracy) <= 3% (we'll run this).
5) Operational: system should maintain <1% error rate and have alerting in the Console for token spikes.

POC timeline (proposed):
- Thu Aug 6: Sign off on MAP assumptions (you)
- Mon Aug 10: Run 48-hour tokens/$ verification job (we'll coordinate start time)
- Wed Aug 12: Review results, adjust batch/cache settings and iterate
- Fri Aug 14: Final MAP acceptance or list of open items

Next steps: please review the attached workbook and tell us whether you want the acceptance gates expressed as tokens/$ or USD per 1k sessions in the formal MAP doc. Also confirm an approximate start time for the 48-hour verification run (we recommend a weekday start at 00:00 UTC to capture typical patterns).

Thanks — Ben and Neha are on the thread for any technical clarifications.
